title: 01 / Pin the point of view
body:
Greatness has a backstory.

CoachRank explores the ideas, decisions and daily work behind remarkable things.

Performance. Business. Creativity. Growth. Coaching.

For ambitious people building something of their own.
notes: Day 1. Pin this introduction. Use the CoachRank wordmark or one strong editorial cover. A single post with a clear invitation to read.

title: 02 / Start with a useful question
body:
Before you redesign your brand, ask someone to explain your offer back to you.

Who is it for? What changes? Why choose you?

The gaps in their answer are a better starting point than a new colour palette.
notes: Day 2. Pair with the article cover. Reply thoughtfully to readers who share a point of confusion. Avoid pasting a sales link into unrelated replies.

title: 03 / Show the report
body:
Your brand may need three clearer decisions.

Our $9 Brand Clarity Assessment gives you a visual report, your next three moves and a seven-day plan.

Pay once. Retake and compare.

Explore the full sample first.
notes: Day 3. Attach a crop of the fictional sample report showing the six dimensions and next moves. Label the image Sample report. Do not present sample scores as a customer result.

title: 04 / A decision worth revisiting
body:
A good outcome can hide a weak decision.

Before your next big call, write down:
1. What you expect.
2. What you are assuming.
3. What would change your mind.

Review the reasoning after the result arrives.
notes: Day 4. Use the decision journal article cover. Invite readers to name one assumption they would test. The useful exercise should stand on its own.

title: 05 / Listen a little longer
body:
A coaching question can open a door. Your next sentence can close it.

After someone answers, try: "What else feels important here?"

Then leave room for the answer.
notes: Day 5. Use a simple text-led visual or the article cover. Join a relevant discussion about listening with a concrete observation.

title: 06 / Give creative work a finish line
body:
Before the next revision, decide what finished means.

Who must understand this?
What must work?
What is outside the scope?

A release standard gives your creative work somewhere to land.
notes: Day 6. Use the creativity article cover. Invite one example of a useful release standard instead of a generic engagement question.

title: 07 / Make the offer clear
body:
Unsure what to fix in your brand first?

24 guided questions. Six dimensions. Three priorities. A seven-day plan.

Brand Clarity Assessment: $9 once, with repeat assessments, report comparisons and downloadable PDFs.

See what is included.
notes: Day 7. Share the product page. Show the report rather than promising revenue. Record useful objections and questions in this record after posting.
